requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline lacked audit=1 (cmd-29b8711f7d304dfc). After grubby update and a full reboot (new boot_id 720242bf... vs fbdf5b2c...), post-reboot /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 and auditctl -s reports 'enabled 1' (cmd-8c287f83d6954256), directly confirming the running kernel booted with audit=1.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (survives a reboot, not just runtime)
requirements.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" was applied and verified in /boot/loader/entries/*.conf for both the normal and rescue BLS entries (cmd-6e4499f827b94a09, cmd-6c3c3f4b33c9445d), meaning it is written to persistent boot configuration rather than a one-off kernel command line edit. A full reboot was then performed (boot_id changed from fbdf5b2c... to 720242bf..., confirmed via connection-drop/timeout followed by successful reconnection: cmd-9e28925d21b143a8, cmd-bd218bc9bb2e41e7, cmd-457d52d5a080470a, cmd-56df0d46b9304288, cmd-a4d19ff5a49b4b25), and the post-reboot kernel cmdline still contains audit=1 with auditd active (cmd-8c287f83d6954256). This directly demonstrates the full healthy-baseline -> disruption -> restoration -> recovered-state transition required for persistence claims.

requirements.requirement: auditd service remains healthy/active before and after the change
requirements.summary: auditd was active in the pre-change baseline (cmd-e9e89992a1b64fa7) and remained active post-reboot with auditctl reporting enabled 1 (cmd-8c287f83d6954256). No failed-services regression observed in the lifecycle snapshots after the executor's work.

overall_summary: The executor persisted audit=1 to both BLS boot entries via grubby, performed an actual reboot of node1 (confirmed by a boot_id change from fbdf5b2c... to 720242bf...), and directly verified post-reboot that /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 with auditd active and auditctl reporting enabled. This satisfies the full pre-change -> disruption -> restoration -> recovered-state evidentiary bar for a persistence/reboot claim, with no unnecessary or unrestored mutations observed.
limitations: The 'audit=1' word placement/order in the BLS options string was not separately validated for conflicts with any other audit= parameter (none was present, so this is a minor gap only).
Rescue kernel entry was verified as edited but not itself booted; only the normal kernel entry's actual boot behavior was directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor mutations were directly tied to the task: (1) grubby --update-kernel=ALL to persist audit=1 (cmd-6e4499f827b94a09) — necessary configuration change; (2) systemd-run --on-active=1 --unit=antrieb-reboot systemctl reboot (cmd-9e28925d21b143a8) — a bounded, self-cleaning transient unit used solely to perform the required reboot verification; it does not persist since the reboot itself clears transient systemd-run units, and the post-executor failed-services snapshot shows none lingering. No unrelated or unnecessary mutations were found; the 3 non-zero-return commands (cmd-bd218bc9bb2e41e7 stream-closed, cmd-457d52d5a080470a and cmd-56df0d46b9304288 connection timeouts) are expected artifacts of the reboot disruption itself, not failures or unnecessary actions. Listening-socket and /tmp diffs between before/after are simply due to new PIDs and systemd-private dirs from the reboot, not executor-caused residue.
